newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-GOETSCHL WINS FIRST GOLD FOR AUSTRIA.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-GOETSCHL WINS FIRST GOLD FOR AUSTRIA.

text.p: Renate Goetschl gave Austria their first gold medal of the Alpine skiing world championships on Saturday, fending off the powerful German favourites to win the women's combined event.

Goetschl, who narrowly missed a medal at the last championships when she finished fourth, clocked a total time of three minutes 3.38 seconds to beat German Olympic downhill champion Katja Seizinger by four hundredths of a second.
It was the first career medal for Goetschl, who has acquired something of a reputation as a maverick on the circuit with regular falls accompanied by a handful of wins.
Seizinger was in turn 0.04 ahead of her compatriot Hilde Gerg while Italy's Morena Gallizio, the leader after Thursday's slalom part of the combined, finished fourth in 3:03.68.
All the medallists were competing in their second race of the day after the regular downhill earlier on Saturday.
The downhill part of the combined was scheduled originally for Thursday but it could not be staged then or on Friday due to high winds and heavy snow in Sestriere.
Gerg and Gallizio could consider themselves unlucky as the wind picked up just before they went down the downhill course.
